title: CKC swarm-safety, EventLedger-atomicity, and pagination hardening (deferred from V2 adversarial review)
origin: New MT created by KERNEL_BUILDER-20260708-025948 during V2 remediation. Captures adversarial-hardening findings from the post-proof review of the CKC media cluster (MT-033/034/035/036) and the intake EventLedger deadlock surfaced by MT-017's proof, so they are not forgotten. These are hardening items BEYOND the proven V1 acceptance of their source MTs; the source MTs' cited acceptance is met and proven on managed PostgreSQL. Do not reopen the source MTs for these.

state_recovery.recovery_rule: This is a deferred hardening tracker. Each finding below is independently implementable and independently provable on managed PostgreSQL. Split into per-finding MTs when activated. Evidence for each finding is in the V2 adversarial-review transcripts recorded in the session.

findings.title: Album unlink/link-edit/reorder record their EventLedger event AFTER tx.commit() in a separate tx
findings.evidence: api/atelier.rs: unlink commit ~3405 then record_event ~3408; link-edit commit ~3515 then event ~3518; reorder commit ~3649 then event ~3662. A crash between commit and event-record persists the membership change with no ledger record, violating the EventLedger-is-authority invariant. Sibling handlers already use record_event_in_tx (e.g. ~3817, ~3995).
findings.remediation: Move the three album-membership events inside the mutation tx via record_event_in_tx(&mut *tx, ...). Add a negative test proving the event and the membership change are atomic (both or neither).

findings.title: Album-list + member pagination order by mutable columns; no DB unique-order guard
findings.evidence: list_character_collections_page orders by mutable updated_at_utc (api/atelier.rs ~2044) which every membership mutation bumps -> skip/duplicate under concurrent agents. Member pagination uses two-statement COUNT+LIMIT/OFFSET (~2078-2101) that drifts under concurrent unlink/reorder. Dense sort_order is app-enforced only (validate_reorder ~2490-2530); no UNIQUE(collection_id, sort_order) at DB (migrations/0031 ~51). Loom sibling already has uq_loom_collection_members_order (migrations/0332 ~73) to reuse.
findings.remediation: Keyset/seek pagination ordered by an immutable key (created_at_utc, collection_id) and (sort_order, asset_id); add a partial/deferrable UNIQUE(collection_id, sort_order) or reuse the Loom ordered-membership pattern. Prove with a concurrent-writer pagination test.

findings.title: Swarm-safety asserted but never raced; large-library test is tiny (3x3)
findings.evidence: atelier_ckc_media_rows_preserve_actor_attribution uses six SEQUENTIAL actors, never two overlapping writes. atelier_ckc_media_album_large_library_pagination seeds only 3 albums / 3 assets, never crosses LIST_CAP=200, never fills a page. FOR UPDATE row locks (api/atelier.rs ~3338,3461,3571) are correct but untested under contention.
findings.remediation: Add a real concurrent-writer race test (tokio::join! two reorders/link-edits on one album; assert serialized + true last-writer attribution) and a true >LIST_CAP large-library pagination test (full-page bound, clamp, stable multi-page traversal).

findings.title: Mutation responses hydrate N+1 (3 sub-queries per member, up to LIST_CAP=200) while holding the FOR UPDATE lock
findings.evidence: media_album_members_from_rows (api/atelier.rs ~2155-2169) runs get_media_review_metadata + list_media_asset_tags + get_media_source_provenance_refs per member, inside the serialization tx (~2388). Up to ~600 round-trips under lock throttles parallel agents.
findings.remediation: Batch the three lookups with ANY($1); hydrate the response AFTER commit.

findings.title: Two store methods hardcode SYSTEM_COLLECTION_ACTOR
findings.evidence: collections.rs update_collection updated_by = SYSTEM_COLLECTION_ACTOR (~630) and remove_images_from_collection unlinked_by = SYSTEM_COLLECTION_ACTOR (~871). CKC API routes thread the real actor and do NOT call these, so MT-036 is satisfied; but a future album-rename/notes route calling update_collection would regress attribution to 'system'.
findings.remediation: Thread the real actor through update_collection and remove_images_from_collection for consistency.

findings.title: Intake batch-apply EventLedger append can deadlock under concurrent writers (no retry)
findings.evidence: During MT-017 proof, atelier_intake_batch_classification_applies_canonical_items_and_links_passed_media failed with PostgreSQL 'deadlock detected' at 'append sheet for batch apply' (atelier_core_data_tests.rs ~2226) when run concurrently with sibling tests; it passes in isolation. MT-020 already added deadlock-retry (40P01/40001) for the prompt-feedback path; the intake batch-apply EventLedger append path lacks it.
findings.remediation: Add MT-020-style deadlock-retry (serialization/deadlock SQLSTATE 40001/40P01) around the intake batch-apply EventLedger append, so concurrent swarm agents doing batch classification do not fail on transient deadlocks. Prove with a concurrent-batch-apply test.

findings.title: Actor attribution trusts unauthenticated x-hsk-actor-id; operator-kind bypasses the model-ops lease entirely
findings.evidence: calling_actor trusts x-hsk-actor-id verbatim (api/atelier.rs ~750-757); validate_model_operation_lease_if_present grants a lease-free pass for x-hsk-actor-kind=operator + x-hsk-actor-id=operator (~7929-7930). FOR UPDATE prevents corruption, but persisted attribution is only as trustworthy as an unauthenticated header, and the lease serialization is optional for a self-declared operator.
findings.remediation: Consistent with the reset brief's LOCAL-FIRST, cooperative-swarm threat model (agents are not adversarial; the Operator owns the host), this is acceptable as-is. If remote/untrusted agents ever come into scope, attribution needs signing and the operator escape hatch needs gating. AWAITING OPERATOR THREAT-MODEL DECISION before any change.

handoff.note: Tracker only. No implementation claimed. Activate per-finding when the Operator schedules hardening; each finding is independently provable on managed PostgreSQL. Source MTs remain proven at their V1 acceptance; do not reopen them for these hardening items.
